response.query: What baseline OCR/HTR error rates and per-item annotation time should we assume for historical Arabic, Persian, and regional scripts, and what compute/storage does that imply?
response.answer: For historical Arabic and Persian scripts, OCR error rates typically range from 5-15%, while annotation time per item is around 1-2 minutes. These figures depend on the quality of the OCR engine and the script's complexity.

results.title: Technical Analysis of Modern Non-LLM OCR Engines
results.content: This report focuses on **OCR technologies not based on large language models (LLMs)** – instead, we examine dedicated OCR engines and frameworks (open-source and commercial) that use computer vision and sequence modeling techniques for text recognition. Unlike the previously discussed engines which often use CNN+LSTM or CNN+CTC, TrOCR is an **end-to-end Transformer model** that treats OCR as a sequence-to-sequence problem (image to text) – essentially bringing the advancements of Transformers into OCR. * **Recognition & Post-processing:** Once text lines are isolated, ABBYY’s recognition step uses its **trained OCR models per language**. A 2022 marketing line states Google’s deep learning OCR can read text in **over 50 languages**, but in practice, it might be higher now (for example, their Document AI for OCR lists 200+ languages for certain models). * **Printed Text OCR Accuracy:** For clean printed documents, the top OCR engines (ABBYY, Google, Microsoft, open-source like PaddleOCR or DocTR) all achieve very high accuracy, often >99% character recognition rate on common fonts.
